Expected Result: Sidebar narrower on input screens (content is minimal there), full width once results exist
Actual Result (live browser): FIXED: new .sidebar-focused-input class (208px -> 168px), toggled by the same boolean setSidebarThisAnalysisVisible() already tracks
Notes: External report's item #10. Root-caused and fixed a genuine rendering hazard found while verifying this live: position:sticky + a CSS transition on width/flex-basis got the sidebar stuck reporting its pre-toggle width indefinitely in this browser engine -- reproduced in isolation, removed the transition (purely cosmetic) rather than ship the risk. A SECOND real bug was caught in a follow-up pre-merge review: the new .sidebar-focused-input rule's higher specificity (two classes) beat the existing 860px mobile breakpoint's sidebar-collapse rule (one class) regardless of media-query nesting, breaking the mobile bottom-nav collapse on every fresh mobile page load -- reproduced by actually resizing to a mobile viewport, fixed by wrapping the rule in @media (min-width:861px). See backend/tests/test_qa_ui_hardening.py.
